Nein, Unternehmen wäre richtig. Auf der englischen Karte steht enterprises, man bekommt also auch die Stimmen der Werften.

Bin mal gespannt was Spielworxx unternimmt um die Fehler zu beheben, aber der ärgerlichste der Fehler (der auf dem Spielplan) kann wohl nicht behoben werden.
Ok, dann stellt sich die Frage, was mit weiteren Karten ist, auf denen „Betrieb“ steht, z.B. John Thorpe und die Gießerei.

Der Fehler auf dem Spielplan ist ärgerlich, aber auch bei „Größer als Erwartungen in Summe der Dividenden“ hätte ich ein Fragezeichen im Gesicht. 
Bin kein professioneller Übersetzer aber zumindest hättest du Fragezeichen im Gesicht und wüsstest, dass es mit den Dividenden zu tun hat, was dich schon mal in die richtige Richtung lenkt. Die andere Übersetzung dagegen ist einfach komplett falsch und irreführend. Gerade bei John Company ist man durch die vielen Regeln stark auf die kleinen Spielhilfen auf dem Material angewiesen.

Ich habe mich auf die deutsche Version auch sehr gefreut und hätte sie bestimmt nicht storniert, wenn ich nicht schon die Englische hätte. Tatsächlich ist aber die Sprachbarriere gar nicht so groß. Die Blackmail-Karten ausgenommen, ist alles im Spiel offene Information und wird sehr gut per Icons oder ganz einfachen kurzen Sätzen erklärt. Bei Leuten die englisch nicht so gut beherrschen ist dann einfach etwas mehr initiale Erklärung nötig (Versprechens- und Black

Die abgebildeten Symbole sollten hilfreich sein, denn wie könnte man diese "falsch übersetzen"?
Die englischen originalen (?) Texte der Karten findet man z. B. auf dem "Tabletop Simulator" bei steam.
Ich weiß natürlich, dass es eine berichtigte deutsche Regelfassung gibt, aber sie liegt dem Spiel nicht bei. Und außerdem ist auch nicht im Regelheft auf mögliche spätere "Richtigstelllungen" im Internet hingewiesen; sie sind so extrem, dass man von "Regeländerungen" der deutschen Regel sprechen muss.

2967694.body:
It's very probable that the designers of the game know about all of this already, but extra feedback never hurts so I figured I'd make a list of strange things I've seen in the rulebook (since I've seen one of the devs in the forum). 🙂

Death of a character
Page 2 under Winning and Losing specifies that if any character reaches 0 health, the game is lost. However page 13 under The dead states "When a player dies in a boss fight, continue fighting." This seems to contradict page 2 and while it does show what to do with minions it doesn't actually state what this means for the character/player. I.e does the character come to life after the boss fight?

Unclear wording
Page 13 under End of Round inside Enemy Turn. "Move action cubes for hen all enemies have...". Should it be "when"? Even then it would be a very strange wording.

Unlocks
On page 22 it is unclear when to tick an "Act IV" box. Since the character boxes should only be ticked when you played that character this implies Act IV

This is a great compendium.  One thing I couldn't find in the rulebook (or on the cards themselves) was a clarification about "minion"-type summons.  For example, the Torch Heads with The Collector.  In the video game, if the Boss is defeated, combat ends and minions vanish.  Does the rulebook specify this?

This is a great compendium.  One thing I couldn't find in the rulebook (or on the cards themselves) was a clarification about "minion"-type summons.  For example, the Torch Heads with The Collector.  In the video game, if the Boss is defeated, combat ends and minions vanish.  Does the rulebook specify this?

I don't think that's true in the board game, summons seem to just be another monster you have to beat to end the encounter.

Adding in another one based on this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_PR-9lc1LdY

What is 0 cost?
Close to the end of the video he poses the question if a dazed/burn is 0 cost or not for the purpose of things like Steam Barrier (or Claw). I can certainly see where that question comes from since slime/dazed/burn/curse are cards without a written cost listed on them (slime has it in the rules, but not the rest). In the digital game 0 cost is distinctly different from not having a cost, and these cards would not interact with anything that specified 0 cost (like scrape) but I can't find anything in the rulebook that clarifies if 0 and nothing is the same for the board game. Another case where StS players would probably assume one thing, and long time board game players might do the same, but newer players might be confused.

Another random thing I saw in that video, which again is not anything unclear but more about general feedback, is that he drew Burning Blood (heal 2 after every

Onwards! This time with something from the TTS cards :)

Act 3 event Winding Halls
The"Embrace Madness choice asks you to "Add two random card rewards to your deck". Should the word reward actually be there? Looking at other cards and effects there is a clear distinction between gaining a card reward which is aways indicated by an icon an which is the standard draw three keep one thing, and a gaining a random card which is just a single card. In this case the text spells out card reward which is never done otherwise, making me think this is a typo in one direction. Either it should be two card reward icons, or just two cards (without the word reward).

That is indeed confusing. The intended behaviour is add the top two cards from your reward deck. I'm guessing they specified reward so it wasn't misinterpreted in a way to grab two rares instead, but that does need to be more clear.

Establishment
RAW this seems to require some bookkeeping. If it lowers the cost of retained cards by one until they leave your hands that should mean that if you retain a card two turn then it costs 2 less, since the effect would trigger and lower the cost by 1 each turn and the "no memory" rule from the book only applies once cards leave your hand. Is this intentional? It brings it closer to the digital version but I also understood things as if the intention was not to have things that just need to be remembered like this.

A bit ambiguous since "costs 1 energy less" could be seen as costing one less than original not one less than current, in which case it wouldn't stack, but certainly not crystal clear.

For poison it says damage is applied at the end of turn.  At a glance this could be misconstrued as end of round. "End of round" is clarified on another page (12) as end of player round. However people quickly looking up poison effect may not read this.  I would suggest rewording to "End of player round" or "Start of enemy turn" for clarity under the poison rules.

For poison it says damage is applied at the end of turn.  At a glance this could be misconstrued as end of round. "End of round" is clarified on another page (12) as end of player round. However people quickly looking up poison effect may not read this.  I would suggest rewording to "End of player round" or "Start of enemy turn" for clarity under the poison rules.
I've seen people make this mistake. Brother's Murph did it in their playthrough vid. We'll figure out a way to address it.

This is a great compendium.  One thing I couldn't find in the rulebook (or on the cards themselves) was a clarification about "minion"-type summons.  For example, the Torch Heads with The Collector.  In the video game, if the Boss is defeated, combat ends and minions vanish.  Does the rulebook specify this?
Hi Chris!
There's no rule for summons running away when an Elite or Boss is defeated. Maybe we should explicitly state they don't run away in the FAQ.

I'll throw in one last random question from me, which is not unclear or a rule book question at all really, but something I am curious about. On page 11 we see how the Sentries will work. Is there any reason that the "main" Sentry attacks differently that the summoned ones? The attack pattern of the Sentries is so recognisable for anyone who has played StS that I was really surprised to see that it was now random (even if it is two and one), but even more surprised that the "main" sentry works differently than the rest and does less damage. So in multiplayer the character in the bottom row faces a sightly different ersion of the elite than the rest. How come?
Because this fight is harder solo and players needed a little help. Note that the Ascension 1 main Sentry works differently.

Solo Difficulty:
Woohoo, I FINALLY beat boss 3 today (solo), after maybe 10 games. I feel this game is really tough for solo play, since you can only really concentrate on one strategy/power, while with 2 players you have 2 possible ways. Example: you concentrate on poison (silent) and end up with the Champ in act 2 - not a chance! Destroyed me like 3 times 😄 With 2 players, you might still have the other strategy that has power early in the combat (poison just takes way too long and cannot compete with all those strength buffs).
So I wonder if there are plans on making solo play easier? Or maybe I just suck (never played the StS video game) - then never mind 😄

Leaving Act 3:
What happens after act 3? Do I heal as usally, before I encounter the heart?
Anything else to keep in mind? :)

Merchant:
At first glance it wasn't clear to me which cards the merchant offers - there are costs for rare cards listed, but I only draw from the normal reward deck. Didn't think of the golden ticket

3352280.body:
I'm down to my last energy and The Guardian is at 2 HP while I'm at 1 HP. He's in defensive stance. And I've got an upgraded strike (does 2 damage) and no block. 

If I don't hit him, he'll kill me on his turn. But if I hit him I'll kill him but will I take the 1 damage as well and die too? Is that correct? Or does the damage only occur if he lives?

Devs Answered:
"Combat ends immediately and you don't take the damage.

The only time combat doesn't end immediately when all monsters are dead is 'on death' abilities that summon an enemy."

A literal reading of the rules would mean that you survive. It says combat ends immediately when all enemies are dead. This would mean that combat ends before the trigger from The Guardian can resolve.

I believe this is different than how the video game works, so I can also see why some players might prefer to play it such that all triggers also resolve before combat ends. But I think that's probably a less common interpretation.

What is the actual rule written on the Guardian?  If you would take damage at the end of your turn, then you do not take it if the enemy dies before then.  I don’t recall the exact wording on the boss.

What is the actual rule written on the Guardian?  If you would take damage at the end of your turn, then you do not take it if the enemy dies before then.  I don’t recall the exact wording on the boss.
"...after you play an attack, take 1 damage."

"...after you play an attack, take 1 damage."

That is a tough call, then…the timing is difficult.  After you play the attack, the Guardian is still alive.  After you RESOLVE the attack, it is not there any more and the rule is not in effect.  I think I would say you survive, but I am not sure.

"...after you play an attack, take 1 damage."

…After you play the attack, the Guardian is still alive…


So you’ll die…

Just like in the video game, the guardian kills you.

The lose of 1 hp is not an attack from him, but you trying to hit him while he has thorns on him and yes that hurts :).

So yes you kill him, but you die trying. 
And then you see Neow again who says to you: "another try?".
And then you are addicted to the game and do another run, because this time you will survive, and then again and again.

That is a tough call, then…the timing is difficult.  After you play the attack, the Guardian is still alive.  After you RESOLVE the attack, it is not there any more and the rule is not in effect.  I think I would say you survive, but I am not sure.

This discussion has come up for other interactions before. In your opinion, at what point in the process is a card considered to have been "played" but not yet "resolved"? And do you believe that triggered abilities are able to be resolved before the card text at that point? Steps for playing a card attached.
The RESOLVE text and the rule that the combat ends immediately tells me that you do the damage and do not take the consequences, unlike the video game.  But I could still see it either way.

I think it's fair to play it either way. The rules aren't entirely equipped to deal with the interaction because there isn't a concrete rule on what order triggers are resolved.

Page 12 of the rules (and listed above) tell us: "Execute  card's printed effect from top to bottom. Any abilities triggered by the card don't take effect until after the card is finished resolving all of its text."

So it's clear the card is played and the enemy is dealt lethal damage. Now there are two simultaneous triggers:
1. After you play an attack, take 1 damage.
2. Combat ends immediately when all enemies are dead.

You could assume the word immediately means to take precedence in the order of triggers. In this scenario you would live.

There is a clue on page 12 about how simultaneous triggers are resolved: "Start of turn abilities - The following abilities trigger in any order the players choose." Obviously this only mentions start of turn abilities, but it seems reasonable to use this ruling for all

Just like in the video game, the guardian kills you.

That is most likely incorrect; whether a triggered ability that is not "On Death" can trigger after the enemy dies is, perhaps, up for debate, however, as has been mentioned previously, combat immediately ends after the last enemy is killed (or leaves combat) and, as the Guardian is always the only enemy, this strongly implies that the lethal attack does not incur damage from Defensive Mode in the board game.

"...after you play an attack, take 1 damage."

…After you play the attack, the Guardian is still alive…


So you’ll die…

This interpretation would require triggered abilities to take place prior to the effect of the card that triggers them, which is the exact opposite of what the rulebook states, and again, after the lethal attack resolves, the combat ends immediately, seemingly leaving no space for triggers to resolve.

I'll be happy to accept a Dev ruling to the contrary, of course, however, for the time being, it is likely

Devs and I are discussing it. There's some tension between combat ending immediately when all enemies are dead, and something I've said before "i guess abilities resolving after death is implicit or on death abilities don't work". Maybe that should only apply to 'on death' abilities.

2821283.body:
Not a rant, just saying that I've been caught multiple times by having overlooked rules, especially those explained in the Icon List or Glossary. So I'm more trying to say how well supported the game rules are, by all the efforts of the designer and publisher.

So do yourself a favour, and read all the material, and have them available at the table in your first games.

Also, the game designer and developers have gone to great lengths to answer the many questions asked here on BGG, and have compiled a very useful FAQ post-publishing. The English language version of all these files can be found on BGG in the Files section, and German versions on the Feuerland Spiel Arche Nova web page.

If you are new to the game, I also suggest the Start Decks the publishers have provided to help get started (optional).
Really this statement should be a pop-up every time someone tries to post a comment on any of the BGG forums.

You shouldn’t assume that the reason people ask questions which are answered in the rulebook, is because they haven’t read the rulebook. It is extremely easy to miss even the simplest of things even if you’re staring right at it. Between the rulebook, glossary, icon sheet, FAQ etc.. there’s like 30-40 pages worth of information to take in and remember. 

So even having all that info handy, many questions are inevitable, originating from thousands and thousands of different people with varying abilities to translate theory into practice. 

… this is the whole point of an open forum.. and more so within the correct “rules section”. It’s like.. I know the answer is buried somewhere within those 35pages of rules.. but I’m not sure exactly where. So I’ll ask a question on bgg. Those who don’t mind helping me out will answer, and those who find it an annoyance, will simply move on. Isn’t it a bit counter productive to add to a post you already deem unnecessary?

Personally, I can understand
I looked everywhere already, what is the rule for determining start player in a solo game? Please help ive had my game setup for two weeks staring at me.

Its a small line between-

- saying to people that they should read the rules and
- trying to help

I feel here with Ark Nova its a special Case and maybe more "easy questions" then in other heavy Eurogames, because more people buy it that are not "heavy Boardgamers"

So all Ark Nova Lovers should be happy that so many people try it :)

We needed some 40 plays of AN to find out, that we misunderstood one symbol: X@. You will find that in particular on those bonus tiles, but sometimes on your zoo board, too. We thought it means get x-times money from your sponsors card rank - but indeed it meant: pay as much money as you like to play a sponsors action with the same value now!

So, ja: it is a good advice to look for those rules calls which came up with the German, and then the UK-Release - spreading now to North America. But do not hesitate to ask anything, as AN is indeed that one more step pretty much of you are taking!

AN needs some guidance, some sort of explaining and citating - but it is worth the efford!

Cheers
Marcel

2848813.body:
I am often very critic about the poor quality of the rulebooks and even more about the amateurism of their French translations. ( see my many posts on this topic )
Here I want to say my admiration to the RuleBook very well written, clear, conceptual enough without  being too abstract and  the quality of the SuperMeeple translation.
Big applause to those who worked of it ( English and French versions ).

Nothing is perfect in this world and there is nevertheless some mistakes on the French translation :
When they translated the text from Animal action level II they added a sentence at the end of the paragraph regarding the extra cost when playing the card form the display : « ( en plus du coût de la carte elle-même ) ». Which means « on top of the price of the card itself». Which is not issue but when you later cut and paste this same text in the Association action level II Conservation project work and in the Sponsor action level II. As nor the Conservation project cards nor the sponsor cards have any price this extra sentence is confusing in both situations ( at least for me during my 1st play ).
Would the English rulebook have used two different wordings for this cost ( additional cost for Animal and extra cost for Association ) they would have seen the difference…

Nevertheless nothing important, it is globally of excellent quality and much better than what many other French publis

Another small error ( English and French ).
Page 15. the sentence « Also no new base conservation projects are added during the game » « Notez qu’aucun nouveau projet de conservation de base ne peut être ajouté pendant la partie » is not 100% true : when you play the White Rhinoceros, you pick a remaining base conservation project you will play later.
A more correct wording would be “Those base conservation projects cannot not be replaced and will remain active until the end of the game” ( as the base conservation project you get with the White rhino will be added later but on the upper line ).

3331080.body:
Took me a while to remember these rules, ones that I messed up my first couple plays. 

Passing Initiative.
You don't have to play the lead card if you have the initiative! You can pass the initiative to the next person in turn order. If everyone with cards in their hand passes consecutively, discard all action cards and end the chapter

Tax
You can tax a loyal city from anywhere, regardless of player control. 

Build
When you build anything in a system that is controlled by anyone other than you, place the piece damaged.

Catapult moves
Planets stop catapult moves just like a gate controlled by someone else does.
You can also double back on your path when dropping off ships when you do a catapult!
Not only that, but you can pass through a bunch of other people's ships in gates if there is a tie for control, since if there's a tie for control nobody controls it! Catapult moves are weird. 

Raid Dice
Raid Dice Limit: You can only collect raid dice if there are defending buildings or if

Here's a couple more:

Excess ship hits carry over to buildings

Raiding only occurs if you have ships left

Quite a few rules only apply to fresh ships
Good list of good catches. Thanks for putting this together. I appreciate this type of reminder periodically!

The limits on prelude actions!

- resources return to the supply at the end of the prelude
- you can’t use a prelude action of a card you secured during that same prelude
And a key rule that I’ve noticed seems easily forgotten by first-time players: you can only declare the Ambition as determined by the card you play.

Raiding only occurs if you have ships left


A good addition to this: While Raiding only happens if you have ships left, damage you do to ships/buildings as Attacker still happens even if all your ships are destroyed by the flame icon hits and interception damage.

You can only build/tax once at a particular starport/city during a single turn. It's an easy one to forget, so I put the new ships and taxed resources onto the city itself to keep track then take/move them off once all building/taxing is done.

When Surpassing, you only need to be higher than the Lead card to use all your pips. Had multiple people think you had to beat all prior cards of the same suit (since that's how many trick-takers work).

If you use a Relic or Psionic to Secure during a Prelude, you cannot use the Prelude action of that card this turn (though the rest of the text still applies). I'm sure I've messed this up myself in early games.

I had the pleasure of playing Arcs for the first time with two others (also their first play) yesterday. These were the questions that came up during our first play to which we were unable to find answers.

1. During your Prelude, can you use Prelude actions on Guild cards acquired during that same Prelude that are not secured from the court (such as stealing from another player)?
Details: Player A had Silver-Tongues (action ... Prelude: You may discard this to steal a Guild card or resource.) as their Prelude began. They used its Prelude ability to steal Relic Fence (action ... Prelude: Once per turn, you may discard 1 resource to gain 1 Relic.) from Player B and then used Relic Fence that same Prelude.
How we played it: We allowed it because it did not break the rule-as-written on page 20 of the rulebook which reads "You cannot use Prelude actions on cards that you secured from the Court in the same Prelude."

2. With two Move actions, can you effectively move "through" a system cont

1. I'd say yes, because it specifically says "you can't use actions on cards you secured from the court." Stealing is not securing from the court.
2. Yes. Movement has no restriction on control. So you can move through.
3. Yes, control is fluid and changes with each action.
4. Yes, you've fired the missiles, they are going to hit something.

All correct

If this helps you and your players, go for it. But there's a reason that rulebooks aren't usually written this way. 

Take a look at the catapult rule you quoted. If you define a few concepts (system, loyal, starport, control, planet, gate) then you can compactly a rule like this. Moreover, you can then change the rule fluidly by adding to or changing these definitions. 

If you instead attempt to write out every single possible interaction of any rules, combinatorics will screw you. You're almost guaranteed to miss some interactions, and even if you do get an exhaustive list, then you'll get a document that nobody can hold in their head for actually playing a game.

Or - is it easier to remember the sum of every two possible numbers, or to learn the definition of addition?

Played a game this past weekend and had a player call my attention to something we had apparently been playing wrong.

Multiple players can surpass so long as their card follows the lead suit and is of a higher value.

Essentially, when an ambition is called, all players following suit will get all action pips on their cards if they follow suit as the declared cards value will be a -0-.    He called my attention to the note in the player aid under 'surpass' in parenthesis:  'Play an action card matching the lead card's suit but with a higher number than it.  (Not every played card!)'

So, say lead card is a 3 Administration.  Player two follows suit and plays a 5, surpassing and gets two actions.  Then player three also follows suit, plays a 4 and gets three actions for surpassing as well.

This makes a HUGE difference in play....I am assuming this is correct?

That’s correct. Just make sure initiative goes to whoever surpassed with the highest number, not necessarily the person who surpassed last. (The way you played before, these would have always been the same person)

Yes, everyone who plays a higher card of the lead suit technically "surpasses" and gets actions from all their pips. Yes, this is a huge thing, especially if not played that way... haha.

First game last night. Lots of fun - it's a good reset back to a simpler rule set (vs. the original with expansions) and feels after that one game to have really good balance. My favorite rule is the double combat benefits to the worms, it adds a lot of excitement.

One question though: The rules are emphatic that you must have a unit in the fight to get a prize. Clearly troops/cubes are units. Clearly daggers are not. But are worms units? One player put in a worm with no cubes to get double 3rd place bonus, and we weren't sure if it was allowed or not. We decided they were, if the rules meant you must have troops they would have said so, but since you can mix in Ix maybe they meant units to mean "troops or dreadnoughts."

Can somebody say for sure what is the intent?

Yes, worms are units.
There are two types of units: troops and sandworms.
Page ten also clarifies that Dreadnoughts are units when using rise of Ix.

Main rulebook, top of page 10:

There are two types of units: troops and sandworms.

The RISE OF IX expansion includes another type of unit, called dreadnoughts.
EDIT: 🥷
The worms aren’t just units… they’re ABSOLUTE UNITS. 😱

Just a recap, there are now three types of units in DI Uprising:
- Troops (cubes)
- Worms
- Dreadnoughts (Rise of Ix)

Please note that some effects ask you to retreat a Unit, but that would NOT apply to worms given that they cannot be in your garrison (ruling by Paul Dennen).

3196416.body:
Hello,

I was just looking through the rulebook of the Dune Imperium: Uprising (DI:U) and I really like how they updated the new Rivals and their rules, especially for the two player (2p) game. I was wondering if anybody thought about ways of backporting these new rules to the base Dune Imperium (DI) game? I would specifically be interested in having a Rival as a third player in a 2p game that competes for the victory and not just blocking spaces passively. This seems as an interesting new approach that was introduced in the DI:U and is missing from the DI. After a quick glance, I don't see why these new rules for the Rivals could not be backported?

Motivation: The new rules of DI:U have retained backwards compatibility for the solo and 2p games with the base DI game, with the so-called Streamlined Rivals that do not compete for the victory. It would be great if they provided a backport of the new rules for Rivals to the base DI game as well. I am playing the DI with my wife most ofte

Following the previously introduced rules for the new Rivals, this is my thinking on the Faction priority lists for the leaders from the DI (when serving as Rivals with the new rules):
- Paul Atreides and Countess Ariana Thorvald could not be used as Rivals.
1. Count Ilban Richese (one dot): Swordmaster value: 9, Faction priority: 1 - Emperor, 2 - Guild, 3 - Bene Gesserit, 4 - Fremen.
2. Earl Memnon Thorvald (one dot): Swordmaster value: 9, Faction priority: 1 - Guild, 2 - Bene Gesserit, 3 - Fremen, 4 - Emperor.
3. Glossu "The Beast" Raban (one dot): Swordmaster value: 8, Faction priority: 1 - Guild, 2 - Fremen, 3 - Emperor, 4 - Bene Gesserit.
4. Duke Leto Atreides (two dots): Swordmaster value: 6, Faction priority: 1 - Fremen, 2 - Bene Gesserit, 3 - Guild, 4 - Emperor.
5. Countess Ariana Thorvald (three dots): Swordmaster value: 5, Faction priority: 1 - Bene Gesserit, 2 - Emperor, 3 - Fremen, 4 - Guild.
6. Baron Vladimir Harkonnen (three dots): Swordmaster value: 4, Faction priority:
Even in DI:U the faction list is rarely used unless there is a tie, and gives a little theme to the rival, and take the power out of the players hand for choosing the influence

I've been playing 2p DI games with backported rivals and I must say they are great! This is far better than the original approach. You really feel like there is a third player and you can make it more or less challenging. We play with expert deployment, since this makes the Rival more "intelligent". My wife really likes this as well, as there is far less friction between us in combat. I would recommend this mode for couples. 🙂

Is there anything you haven't already mentioned that you included over more plays to clean up this back port?

And did you include any other 2p house hagal cards other than the shuffle card?

Also, how do the rivals gain resources, do you no longer ignore all the effects on the board?

Here's the one my wife and I use. I took what you did and springboard off of it.

Dune Imperium Rivals Back-Port

Setup
1. Put three troops in its garrison. 
2. Place 1 water in its supply. 
3. Give it 1 intrigue card
4. Set its Swordmaster (third Agent) next to the game board. 
5. Place one of its discs on the score track.
6. Remove all 2p House Hagal cards except for the reshuffle card.

Note:
Paul Atreides and Helena Richese cannot be played as Rivals.

Swordmaster
- A Rival will first accumulate resources to gain a Swordmaster. As soon as it has a number of total resources equal to its Swordmaster value, it spends those resources to gain its Swordmaster. If it has more than enough resources for its Swordmaster, it will first spend Solari, then Spice, then Intrigue cards, then Water (keeping any leftovers).
    - 1 dot —> 9 SM Value
    - 2 dots —> 7 SM Value
    - 3 dots —> 5 SM Value
- Once a Rival has its Swordmaster, it begins spending its resources to earn Victory Points
- Conv

I really enjoyed the advanced rivals in DI:U but having played the original DI recently with the "solo play" rivals, I found that there isn't much of a difference! 

They gain points, use the signet ring, have a fixed turn for swordmaster (based on your desired difficulty). What's not to like? 🙂 So it works out of the box for 2P, it's just incorrectly labeled as "solo play".

Facing off against 2 bots was pretty challenging. It also worked well as a co-op (2 humans vs 2 bots, team with most total points at the end wins).

One thing that could be nicer would be to backport the bot leader cards, as their abilities are a bit more tuned to this setting.

Hi everyone, it looks like the Dire Wolf team just updated their Official Dune Imperium FAQ this week to include content from Uprising. 

I've integrated the new entries into my Unofficial FAQ doc, which also contains links to various edge cases and questions answered elsewhere (BGG threads, Discord, etc.). 

Of note is an additional Endgame tiebreaker for when you get all the way down to troops in garrison:

"In the extremely rare case that the endgame tiebreakers listed in the rulebook aren’t enough to resolve a tie, the final tiebreaker is the player who most recently took a Reveal turn."

"In the extremely rare case that the endgame tiebreakers listed in the rulebook aren’t enough to resolve a tie, the final tiebreaker is the player who most recently took a Reveal turn."

What's the reason for that to be considered a tiebreaker?  🤔
Just removes the possibilities of tied games totally instead of mostly totally. That said, out of 100+ games, I haven't ever even hit the Water part of the tiebreaker.
Note that new entries to ’s Official FAQ are marked with an asterisk.

Just removes the possibilities of tied games totally instead of mostly totally. That said, out of 100+ games, I haven't ever even hit the Water part of the tiebreaker.

Yeah, but why "most recent reveal turn" rather than "first to take a reveal turn"?  Or not "player with First Player token" or any number of other things that could be used as an absolute tie-breaker?
Could literally just be a random (and final) qualifier after you’ve used all the other ones?

It might never occur as it should be extremely rare...
Anyway I can see two reasons:
1. You are probably last player in the last Round of the game which put you at a disadvantage!

Hello, I want to know what is this mean . 
"-Is Muad’Dib’s passive ability triggered if one of his Allies has a Sandworm in the conflict?
-He only has shared ownership with the Ally he activated during his Reveal turn. If that Ally has a worm, then so does Muad’Dib and he draws his Intrigue card."

3341774.body: I play the Shrieking Amphiptere. During Explore I tuck a dragoon with a cost of 1 gold and 1 coin. Would I receive a gold and a coin?
You would receive exactly 1 resource (milk, gold, meat, or gem) from the cost of the dragon, so in this case you would receive 1 gold.

I play the Shrieking Amphiptere. During Explore I tuck a dragoon with a cost of 1 gold and 1 coin. Would I receive a gold and a coin?
No.

A) You only receive one thing for the one icon in the Amphiptere's ability, not both.
B) The wild resource icon only covers the four resources, not coins nor eggs, so you can only get meat/gold/crystal/milk from it.

In this case, you'd get gold. Other dragons could give you a choice of which resource to get, but you'd still only get one resource (or none if the tucked dragon's cost doesn't include any resources).

If you are looking for a general overview of how the game works, check the rulebook and other materials in the download section on CGE web, or watch the official How to Play video:

Don’t be surprised by the length of this FAQ. It’s not meant to be read from start to finish, but to help you quickly find answers about a specific card or rule. Some information may repeat what’s already in the rulebook, but phrased in a way that can make it easier to understand to some. You’ll also notice certain clarifications appearing more than once, since related notes are listed under each relevant entry for easier searching.

The FAQ for the SETI: Space Agencies expansion can be found in a separate threa

INDIVIDUAL CARDS

🚀 #1 Pioneer 11 MIssion / #2 Mariner 10 Mission / #3 Voyager 2 Mission / #4 Galileo Mission
Despite the card costing 0 credits, playing it for its effects is still considered a main action.

“Visiting a planet” requires you to move your probe to a space with that planet. When you have a probe on a space with one of the planets required by the mission when you play the card, you can’t cover the mission reward. You need to move to the space with that planet again to trigger it. 

Having an orbiter or lander at the required planet doesn’t qualify as visiting the planet either. 

🚀 #9 Falcon Heavy
By default you are limited to having no more than 1 probe in space (on the Solar system board) at once. The two launches on this card ignore this limit, so if you have 1 probe in space already when play this card, you will end up with 3 probes in space (or even 4 probes if you have the orange tech that increases the limit and you had 2 probes in space prior to playing this car

Still don't get it about conditional missions. They work like triggerable? You need to fulfill after you play, or if you have met condition, you can get reward right away? Example: I have two Landers. Next time I play conditional mission "have 2 Landers". Am I qualified?
Yes. 
▪️ The conditional missions require certain state of the game, usually requiring you to accumulate certain amount of something (for example you having at least 2 landers, having at least 3 purple traces, etc.). 
▪️ The triggerable missions require you to perform a certain kind of activity, and when you do, they trigger (for example perform a Scan action, gain a Blue trace, visit a particular planet). They won't trigger for things you have done prior to playing the card.

These terms are all frequently confused but are well defined in the rulebook. This might be an area where thematic intuition (you probably want to put something into orbit before you land it) and gameplay mechanics are in semi-conflict. Just think of landing as encompassing everything involved with landing.

"Probe": This term is defined on page 8 of the rulebook under the Launch a Probe action: "Take one of your probe figures, and place it on the Earth space of the solar system board." The icon for probe is a black/dark grey 🛰️ icon. (By contrast the icon for an orbiter is green).  In addition: "“In space” is anywhere in the rings of the solar system board. By contrast, figures on the planetary board are not “probes in space”" (emphasis added)

A Probe must be at a planet on the planetary board to turn into an Orbiter or a Lander: "Having a probe at a planet gives you an option to turn it into aor a  , as
